title: The Mahavastu — the Sanskrit text
textType: Monastic narrative in prose and verse
attributionNote: The Mahāvastu-avādana of the Mahāsāṃghika-Lokottaravāda school, transmitted without an author as part of that school's discipline: its Sanskrit is a mixed dialect, older in its verses and modernised in the prose that frames them. GRETIL's e-text follows Émile Senart's edition in three volumes (Paris 1882–1897) and was input by Emmanuel Fauré.
description: The Mahāvastu is the great story of the Buddha's career as the Mahāsāṃghikas told it: previous Buddhas and the vow that sets the Bodhisattva on the way, his lives in the heavens and the descent into the world, the birth and the naming of Gotama, the palaces, the four encounters, the departure and the six years of effort, the awakening, and the first conversions, with the lives of the first disciples told around them. Its chapters on the ten stages of the Bodhisattva and on the pomp of the birth are among the earliest Mahayana material to survive in the original, and its narrative is the richest of the older biographies.
historicalContext: The work's school disappeared, but its text was preserved in the manuscripts found in Nepal; Senart's edition made it the principal witness to the Sanskrit of the Mahāsāṃghika canon, and it is read today beside the Pali Mahāvagga and the Lalitavistara for what the schools of early Buddhism shared and where they parted.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: the whole work in Senart's three volumes, 1,324 sections, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one volume at a time. The file marks each volume above its text and wraps each reference in underscores; the reader drops the apparatus and keeps the section. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
